record.original_question: Given a positive distance d and a plane figure or space body, determine the maximum size of a set of points with pairwise distances at least d, determine the minimum size of a set of points that d-covers the figure in the sense that every added point lies within distance d of one of the chosen points, and study the corresponding variants for interior points only, boundary points only, or strict inequalities.

evidence.quote: More generally: let d > o. Questions: (a) Which is the maximum number of points included in a plane figure (a space body) such that the distance between any two points is greater or equal than d? (b) Which is the minimum number of points ... (c) Other variants ... (III) These are generally open (unsolved) questions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d>0$ be a fixed positive real number, and let $F\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ (for $n=2$ or $n=3$) be a compact set (a plane figure or a body in space). Investigate the following extremal quantities and their variants:

(a) Packing number. Determine
$$P(F,d) \;=\; \max\Bigl\{\,|S|\;:\;S\subseteq F,\ \|x-y\|\ge d\ \text{for all distinct } x,y\in S\Bigr\}.$$

(b) Covering number. Determine
$$C(F,d) \;=\; \min\Bigl\{\,|T|\;:\;T\subseteq F,\ \forall z\in F\ \exists t\in T\ \text{with } \|z-t\|\le d\Bigr\},$$
i.e.\ the minimum number of points of $F$ whose closed $d$-neighborhoods cover $F$.

(c) Variants. Study the corresponding problems when:
 (i) the points are required to lie only in the interior $\mathrm{int}(F)$;
 (ii) the points are required to lie only on the boundary $\partial F$;
 (iii) the inequality $\|x-y\|\ge d$ in (a) is replaced by the strict inequality $\|x-y\|>d$, and analogously $\|z-t\|\le d$ in (b) is replaced by $\|z-t\|<d$.

For each variant and each natural class of figures or bodies $F$ (for instance disks, squares, regular polygons, balls, cubes, regular polytopes), give exact values, sharp asymptotics, or sharp bounds, together with characterizations of the extremal configurations.
artifact.status_search_result: Generalized packing and covering problems for points in a given figure or body, asking for maximum d-separated sets or minimum d-covers (with interior/boundary/strict-inequality variants), constitute a classical family in discrete and combinatorial geometry. While many special cases (e.g., packings in squares, disks, cubes) have been studied extensively, the general problem in the stated form remains open in most cases, with only sporadic exact results known.

status_evidence.title: Packing problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Many of these problems, when the container size is increased in all directions, become equivalent to the problem of packing objects as densely as possible in infinite Euclidean space. Optimal packings in squares, circles and cubes have been determined only for small numbers of points.
status_evidence.claim: General packing problems in plane figures and bodies are largely unsolved except for small cases.

status_evidence.title: Covering problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Covering problems are minimization problems and usually integer linear programs, whose dual problems are called packing problems. Exact solutions are known only for specific cases.
status_evidence.claim: Covering numbers of general figures are not known in closed form.
